chapter: Return to New Orleans and Sharkey
title: Leading Sharkey's band, the television show and quitting
summary: He tells of the four-piece Preview job, how Sharkey's band formed at the Famous Door, their fame, a dispute over free radio work, and leaving to open a Baton Rouge club.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: I was a little bit of a band called Bill Gruber. So they only wanted a four piece band because it was a small stage, smaller than the famous door, see. So they only had four pieces. So I had to leave Sharky go and let the Bouchard go, see. So it was trombone, piano, drums and bass. So when I got finished there, Sharky, Monk Hazel, you know how Sharky got in the famous store? Monk Hazel told Hip, he said, man why don't you put a Dixieland band in this? He said, you're not making money with that Spanish band and all that stuff, put a Dixieland band in here. So he said, why don't you get Sharky to make up a band? So he made up a band, he got Jeff Riddick, Lester Bouchard, Jake Martin, and he had Diggalane, you know, and he had a girl singer, see. So Diggalane, something happened to him, so he called me up and he said, Santa, you want to help me out? I said, yeah, I'm not doing nothing right now. He says, Diggalane got sick or he quit or something like that, I don't know what the hell he said. So, I helped him out, then we, I stood there for a couple of years with him. So, you weren't there when we had the jam session at the auditorium? No, I don't think so. No, Roger was, see. So, I went out and got tickets made and all that stuff, we rent the auditorium and all that stuff. And then Sharky got big, you know, we got the first television show here, see. We played at the Hibernia Bank, up on Tampa, Florida, that was on the move to Royal Street. So, he got, remember we played the boat for D'Antoni, you know, the boat, Banana boat. Then he got so big, his wife started saying, you know, Shark's the king now. I said, that's right. I said, without the band, you can't be the king. The band's got to help you. I said, just like me or anybody else. He said, you can't play by yourself. Just like practicing home, you got to have a band behind you. I said, Sharky don't need you or need you or need nobody. I said, no. So, then Sharky got a, some radio station called and said, say, Sharky, would you like to play, I said, like United Front or something else, for free for about fifteen weeks, you know. I said, Sharky, I'll tell you what I'll do. I'll play two weeks. After two weeks you get Tony Amarica playing the next two weeks with somebody else, see. He said, well, that's how you feel? He said, you can take your notice. I said, that's right. So, I took my notice, I went to the dream room for a little while, then I went to Baton Rouge and opened my own club up. I could have made money in Baton Rouge if they didn't close me at twelve o'clock, the curfew, what kind of school was it, you see.
